la:noun:solitudo.gloss: An instance of being alone; loneliness, solitariness, solitude, privacy
senses: An instance of being alone; loneliness, solitariness, solitude, privacy
A state of want, destitution, deprivation
la:noun:solitudo.html:
sōlĭtūdo, ĭnis, f.
solus
,
a being alone or solitary, loneliness, solitariness, solitude (of a person or place); a lonely place, desert, wilderness (class. in sing. and plur.; cf.: secretum, secessus).
In gen.: ampla domus dedecori saepe domino fit, si est in eā solitudo,: si aliquis nos deus ex hac hominum frequentiā tolleret et in solitudine uspiam collocaret,; so (opp. frequentia) ; opp. celebritas,; : audistis, quae solitudo in agris esset, quae vastitas, quae fuga aratorum, quam deserta, quam relicta omnia,; cf.: quācumque venis, fuga est et ingens Circa te solitudo,: solitudo ante ostium,: ubi postquam solitudinem intellexit,: erat ab oratoribus quaedam in foro solitudo,: neque vero hic non contemptus est a tyrannis atque ejus solitudo,: mihi solitudo et recessus provincia est,: in aliquā desertissimā solitudine,: Sigambri se in solitudinem ac silvas abdiderant,: an malitis hanc solitudinem vestram quam urbem hostium esse? solitary, desert place (Rome), : delere omne Latium, vastas inde solitudines facere,; cf. : nec umquam ex solitudine suā prodeuntem, nisi ut solitudinem faceret,: ubi solitudinem faciunt, pacem appellant,; ; ; : nivosae solitudini cohaerentes,bordering on,.— With gen.: in hac omnis humani cultūs solitudine,.—Plur., ; ; : solitudines renuntiavere missi milites ad explorandum,; ; ; .—
In partic., analog. to the Gr. ἐρημία, in respect of something wanting, a being left alone or deserted, a state of want, destitution, deprivation: per hujus (orbae) solitudinem Te obtestor,; cf.: liberorum solitudo,: liberorum ac parentum solitudo,: Caesenniae viduitas ac solitudo,; : solitudo atque inopia,; cf. : Messalina tribus omnino comitantibus (id repente solitudinis erat) spatium urbis pedibus emensa,: magistratuum,

senses: throne, chair of state, official seat
la:noun:solium.html:
sŏlĭum, ii, n.
from the root sol, kindr. with sed, sedeo
,
a seat.
Most usu. of gods, kings, or other distinguished personages.
Lit., a seat, chair of state, throne (cf.: thronus, tribunal): regali in solio sedens,: domus regia et in domo regale solium,; cf.: solio rex infit ab alto,: solio tum Juppiter aureo Surgit,; so, Jovis,; : divinum,: deorum solia,: regale (Jovis),: sedens in solio consulantibus respondere (of solicitors),; : sedet Sollemni solio,: acernum,: eburnum, i. e. sella curulis,; .—
Meton. like our throne, for rule, sway, dominion (mostly poet.): pristina majestas soliorum et sceptra superba,; cf.: solio sceptroque potitur,; cf. ; ; : solio avorum aliquem depellere,; Claud. IV. Cons. Hon. 213: Demetrium in paterno solio locaturi,: Pacorum avito Arsacidarum solio depulsuri,: paternum solium per vim, per arma capere,.—
A tub, esp. for bathing, ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; .—For other purposes, .—
A stone coffin for persons of distinction, a sarcophagus: solium Porphyretici marmoris,; cf. ; ; Inscr. Marin. Fratr. Arv. p. 343 al.

la:other:Soli.gloss: Soli (a city in Cilicia, in modern Turkey)
senses: Soli (a city in Cilicia, in modern Turkey)
la:other:Soli.html:
Sŏli (collat. form Soloe, ; ), ōrum, m., = Σόλοι.
A town of Cilicia, afterwards called Pompeiopolis, now Mezetli, ; ; .—Hence, Sŏleus, ei, m., = Σολεύς, of Soli: Milon,.—
A town of Cyprus, now Solia, (Jan. Soloe).

la:adj:solidus.html:
sŏlĭdus, a, um (contr. collat. form sol-dus, a, um, ; ), adj.
Sanscr. sarvas, all; Gr. ὅλος, whole; old Lat. sollus; cf. sollistimus
,
firm, dense, compact, not hollow, solid (class.).
Lit.: individua et solida corpora (sc. ἀτόμοι), ; cf. : terra solida et globosa,: columna aurea (opp. extrinsecus inaurata),; cf. cornua (opp. cava),: lapides,: corpus,: paries vel solidus vel fornicatus,: sphaera solida atque plena,; cf.: crateres auro solidi,: ex solido elephanto,; ; : aera,: telum solidum nodis,: vasa auro solida,; : solidum ex auro signum,: nunc solida est tellus, quae lacus ante fuit,; so, ripa,: sedes (opp. aër),: navis ad ferendum incursum maris solida,: sit solidum quodcumque subest,: solidus cibus, solid food, as opposed to fluid, . —Comp.: solidior caseus factus,. —Sup.: solidissima materiaï corpora (opp. mollia),; : tellus,.—Subst.: sŏlĭdum, i, n., a solid substance, solidity: cum duae formae praestantes sint, ex solidis globus, ex planis autem circulus aut orbis,: nihil tangi potest, quod careat solido,; cf.: quae (species deorum) nihil concreti habeat, nihil solidi, nihil expressi,: inane abscindere soldo,; cf. : fossa fit ad solidum,to the solid ground, to the bottom,: finditur in solidum cuneis via,into the hard wood,; : neque fundamenta (amphitheatri) per solidum subdidit,: solido procedebat elephas in pontem,on solid ground,.—
Transf. (opp. to that which is divided, scattered, or in parts), whole, complete, entire (= integer, totus): usurā, nec eā solidā, contentus est,: militia semestri solidum stipendium accipere,: solida taurorum viscera,: ut solidos hauriant (serpentes) cervos taurosque,: quibus solida ungula,: motus terrae quasdam (civitates) solidas absorbuit,: ut decies solidum exsorberet,i. e. at once, in one draught,: decem annos solidos errasse, Varr. ap. ; cf.: partem solido demere de die,: annus,: hora,: parum solidum consulatum explere,incomplete,: vos, quibus...solidae suo stant robore vires,.—As substt.
In gen.: sŏlĭdum, i, n., the whole sum: ita bona veneant, ut solidum suum cuique solvatur,; ; ; ; —
In partic.: sŏlĭdus, i, m. (sc. nummus), in the time of the emperors a gold coin, at first called aureus, and worth about twenty-five denarii, afterwards reduced nearly one half in value, ; ; ; ; ; ; ; Esd. 2, 69; .—
Trop., sound, solid, substantial, genuine, true, real (in this sense a favorite word with Cic.; syn.: firmus, constans, stabilis; opp. inanis, levis, vanus, mobilis, etc.): solida et perpetua fides,; so, fides,: solida et robusta et assidua frequentia,: solida atque robusta eloquentia,: solida ac virilis ingenii vis,: est enim gloria solida quaedam res et expressa, non adumbrata,: judicia solida et expressa,: justitiae effigies,: quod appellant honestum, non tam solido quam splendido nomine,: suavitas austera et solida,: solida veraque laus,; cf.: solida laus ac vera dignitas,: gloria (with vera),: nostra gloria, cum sit ex solido, : nulla utilitas (with puerilis delectatio),: salus,: gratia,; : beneficium,: gaudium,: libertas,; : fides,: mens,firm, determined,: solidum opus doctrinae,, ext. 1: in solidiore aliquo scripti genere,: gravior solidiorque sententia,: virtus,; , ext. 5: vinum,fin.— Neutr. absol.: quibus ex rebus nihil est, quod solidum tenere possis,: multos in solido rursus Fortuna locavit,in safety,; cf.: praesentia bona nondum tota in solido sunt,: nostra gloria, cum sit ex solido,: ut salus ejus locetur in solido,.—Hence, adv., in two forms.
sŏlĭdum (very rare), soundly, thoroughly: dinoscere cautus Quid solidum crepet,: Venus irata solidum,.—
sŏlĭdē (not in Cic.).
(Acc. to I.) Densely, closely, solidly: solide et crassis viminibus contexta cista,: solide natus est,i. e. without a hollow place, without wind in one's inside,.—Comp.: concreta aqua,.—
(Acc. to II.) Surely, wholly, fully, truly: neque, natus necne is fuerit, id solide scio,; ; Ter And. 5, 5, 8; ; .

la:noun:solidus.gloss: A solidus: a Roman ~23-carat gold coin introduced by Diocletian in AD 301.
senses: A solidus: a Roman ~23-carat gold coin introduced by Diocletian in AD 301.
A bezant: the solidus's debased Byzantine successors.
A shilling, as a unit of account or silver coin.

la:verb:solido.gloss: to make, or become solid, firm, etc.
senses: to make, or become solid, firm, etc.
la:verb:solido.html:
sŏlĭdo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
id.
,
to make firm, dense, or solid; to make whole or sound; to strengthen, fasten together (not ante-Aug., and for the most part only in the pass.; cf.: compono, reficio, stabilio).
Lit.: (area) cretā solidanda,: locus fistucationibus solidetur,: terra aëre,: aedificia sine trabibus,; cf. muri,: ossa fracta,; ; cf.: hi (nervi) incisi solidantur,; : cartilago,: fistulae stanno, et saep.—Poet.: facies solidata veneno,i. e. against decay,.—
Trop.
To confirm, establish: rem Romanam,: imperium Romanum ex diuturnā convulsione solidatum, Auct. Pan. ad Const. 1: illud etiam constitutione solidamus, ut, etc., establish, ordain, Cod. Th. 15, 9, 1.—
To unite: viro uxorem unius corporis compage,.—
To correct: rationes, Ps.-Ascon. ap. .

la:verb:solito.html:
sŏlĭto, āvi, 1,
v. freq. n. [soleo], to be much accustomed or wont: Scipionem Africanum solitavisse in Capitolium ventitare,.

senses: the whole (as opposed to a share)
la:noun:soliditas.html:
sŏlĭdĭtas, ātis, f.
id.
.
Lit., solidness, solidity (good prose), ; ; ; ; .—
Transf. (post-Aug.).
Thickness, ; . —
Solidity, firmness, ; .— Hence, plur. concr.: soliditates, firm or solid masses, .—
In jurid. Lat., the whole, entirety (opp. a share, part): possessionis, etc.,; ; Bip.: hereditas universorum soliditas singulorum,, Serm. 14, 41.

la:adj:solitarius.html:
sōlĭtārĭus, a, um, adj.
solus
,
alone, by itself, lonely, solitary (class.; syn. singularis): natura solitarium nihil amat,: quoniam solitaria non posset virtus ad ea, quae summa sunt, pervenire, conjuncta et consociata cum alterā perveniret,: quae (natura) non solitaria sit neque simplex, sed cum alio juncta atque conexa,: deus desertus ac solitarius,; : hae apes non sunt solitaria natura, ut aquilae, sed ut homines,: solitarius homo atque in agro vitam agens,living by himself,: solitaria et velut umbratilis vita,: solitarium aliquod aut rarum judicatum afferre,: distentus solitariā cenā,i. e. with a dinner which he has taken by himself,: modo id egit,i. e. nothing else,: imperium,absolute,: hominem solitarium tres tam validos

evitasse juvenes, .— Pleon.: solus ac solitarius,.

la:adj:solivagus.html:
sōlĭvăgus, a, um, adj.
solus - vagor
(Ciceron.).
Lit., wandering or roving alone; of animals that lead a solitary life: earum (bestiarum) partim solivagas, partim congregatas,.—Of persons: non est enim singulare nec solivagum genus hoc (hominum),: (elephanti) minume ex omnibus solivagi,; v. solitarius.—
Transf., alone, by itself, single, solitary (rare): caelo solivago et volubili et in orbem incitato,: solivaga, cognitio et jejuna,contracted,: virginitas,standing alone, incomparable,.

la:noun:solitas.html:
sōlĭtas, ātis, f.
solus
,
a being alone, loneliness, solitude (ante- and post-class. for solitudo): tuam solitatem memorans, Att. ap. (Trag. Rel. p. 153 Rib.); ; ; .
